headline: On orchestration and scheduling, the v5.0 proposal is not an optimizer — it is a backward-arithmetic display. Its `optimizeEvent` computes each item's start time independently from serve time, never checks device contention in the time dimension, never re-plans, and allocates space with no time dimension at all; the two loops never exchange a single value. Our shipped `planSchedule` + `schedulePlacements` already do resource-constrained placement with slack, per-slot floors, hook counting, bath-temperature exclusivity, a device temperature-ceiling refusal, and six typed conflict reasons — and our approved-but-unbuilt Phase 3a adds the move ladder, hard safety floors and the AI `action_id` contract that v5.0 has no equivalent of. Three ideas are worth harvesting (cooler-as-buffer, device-failure re-plan, consumables predictor); every number attached to them is uncited, and one class of number — sous-vide duration — is a safety value the proposal generates by multiplication.
isItSmarter:
Worse, decisively, and it is not close.

**Time.** v5.0 §5.2: `let cookEndTime = new Date(globalServeTime.getTime() - (item.required_resting_mins * 60000)); let cookStartTime = new Date(cookEndTime.getTime() - (item.required_cook_time_mins * 60000));` — inside `for (let item of menu)`, with `equipment` never referenced in that loop. Every item is scheduled as if it were alone. Two briskets on one one-shelf smoker both get 11:00. No contention detection, no slack, no re-plan. Our `app.js:3858 planSchedule(stages, serveMs)` does the same subtraction *per stage of a multi-stage chain*, then `app.js:3969 schedulePlacements(computed, scope)` runs a real placement pass: sorts per device by `(a.slackMs-b.slackMs) || ((b.demandCm2||0)-(a.demandCm2||0))`, tries `latestFinishMs` then every earlier boundary where a placed item begins, tests with `_windowFits` at every demand-change instant, records `slackMs`, and `app.js:7086` shifts the whole stage chain earlier by that slack. v5.0's engine cannot represent a multi-stage item at all — it has exactly one `required_cook_time_mins` per item, so it cannot schedule its own §3.2 flagship recipe (smoke 2 h → sous-vide 24 h → grill 10 min).

**Space.** v5.0's allocator is time-blind: `spatialAllocation[i] += item.area_required_cm2` is never decremented, so an item that comes off at 13:00 never frees its shelf for one entering at 14:00, and the engine `throw`s `"חסימת נפח"` on plans that are trivially feasible by staggering. Our `app.js:528 packDevice` replays chronologically and releases: `sl.occ=sl.occ.filter(function(o){ if(o.end<=e.start){ sl.free+=o.cm2; return false; } return true; })`.

**Hanging.** v5.0: `if (item.placement_preference === "HANGING" && equipment.supports_hanging) { hangingUsed++; allocated = true; }` — `hangingUsed` is incremented and never compared to anything. An offset with `supports_hanging: true` accepts infinite salami. Ours: `itemOccupancy` returns `{mode:'hang', hooks:1}` gated on `deviceCanHang(dev)` (per-device, not global), and `schedulePlacements` runs `_windowFits(placed.filter(p=>p.mode==='hang'), r.startMs, r.endMs, 1, cap.hooks)` → `reason:'hooks'`. Ours is also derived from the recipe (`spec.hang`), not from `placement_preference` — a salami must hang; it is not a user preference.

**The sort is the tell.** `scheduleTimeline.sort((a, b) => a.action_start_entry.localeCompare(b.action_start_entry))` sorts locale-formatted `HH:mm` strings. That breaks precisely on this product's flagship case: an 8–14 h brisket for a lunch serve starts the previous evening, and "21:30" sorts after "06:00". Our app models this explicitly — `app.js:7020` `// pick the serve day (night / next-day cooks)` with `serveDateKey()`, plus `fmtClockRel(preheat, serve)`. Sorting a `Date` would have been shorter and correct; sorting a display string reveals the object is a render record, not a schedule. Nothing downstream reads the order anyway.

**The wrap point contradicts the proposal's own data.** Code: `action_wrap_stall: new Date(cookStartTime.getTime() + (item.required_cook_time_mins * 0.6 * 60000))`. Its own §3.3 table: `חובה לעטוף ב-71°C (The Stall)`. A temperature and a fixed 60% of elapsed time coincide only by luck. We model it as physics: `app.js:6754 copilotStallInfo(tempC)` → `phase = (t<65?'below' : (t<=77?'stall':'above'))`, grounded in the app's vetted troubleshooting content.

**And `required_cook_time_mins` is an input.** The engine does not estimate cook time; it is handed it and subtracts. There is no preheat/come-up either — our `preheatMinutes()` (45 min default) emits a preheat row and a notification at `app.js:7104`.

Where it is genuinely ahead of us: it *names* three things we have not built — a holding vessel as a schedule buffer, device-failure re-planning, and a consumables predictor. But `allocateFleetAndSpace` and `handleDeviceFailure` are literally `{ /* ... */ }` stubs and `processTelemetry` is a comment block. Those are intentions, not mechanisms — and two of the three (fleet reassignment, hold) are already in our approved Phase 3a §3.3 ladder `share → wood-swap → reassign → cook-early-and-hold → advise`.

adopt.item: The consumables shopping-list OUTPUT SHAPE (§6.4): per-device-type fuel mass + metres of butcher paper, derived from planned cook-hours × device class, surfaced as a pre-event shopping line.
adopt.why: A real user need we do not serve at all. `equipPlan` (app.js ~973-986) sets only `fuelNote`/`refuelEveryMin`, and gap-status D4 records that cook stages carry no equipment-specific instruction. The scheduler already knows every stage's device and duration — `schedulePlacements` has `devId`, `startMs`, `endMs` per stage — so the input to this calculation already exists and is currently thrown away. Adopting the shape costs nothing and touches no safety value.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: New pure function over `schedulePlacements(computed, scope).placements` grouped by `devId`, rendered next to the existing work-plan output built by `workPlanHtml(computed, preheat, serve)` (app.js:7118). Device class comes from `equipList()`/`propOf(dev,...)`, already used by `deviceCapacity`/`deviceCanReach`.

adopt.item: The explicit `safetyBuffer = 1.2` convention — any consumption/quantity estimate shown to a user is inflated 20% and labelled as an estimate.
adopt.why: We already have a strong unknown-vs-zero discipline in occupancy (`cm2: null` never masquerades as 0; `out.pctFloor` marks a percentage as a floor), but nothing equivalent for consumables. Under-buying fuel strands a cook mid-brisket — asymmetric harm — so a named margin constant is the right shape, matching how we already treat `FIT_SLOT_TOL`/`FIT_HARD_FACTOR` as named tolerances rather than inline magic numbers.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: Same new consumables function; declared as a TOP-LEVEL named const alongside `SCHED_PULL_MAX_MS` (app.js:3945) and `FIT_SLOT_TOL`/`FIT_HARD_FACTOR`.

adapt.item: The insulated cooler / faux-cambro as a scheduling BUFFER (§1.2, §5.4, §6.2) and the `events.has_cooler_box` flag.
adapt.why: The single best idea in the proposal on my lens, because it names the exact entity our own scheduler admits is missing. `schedulePlacements` bounds its earlier-pull with a comment that says so in as many words: "Moving a cook earlier is safe for time and temperature, but the item then finishes early and has to wait, and this app cannot yet say WHERE it waits (the hold / refrigerate spine is Phase 3). An unbounded pull is arithmetically valid and practically absurd" — hence the hard constant `SCHED_PULL_MAX_MS = 2*3600e3`. A modelled holding vessel is what would turn that constant into a computed bound, letting the placer resolve contention it currently refuses with `reason:'pull-too-far'`.
adapt.whatMustChange: Three things, all non-negotiable. (1) The proposal's rule — `הגעה ליעד + זמן עד הגשה > מנוחה + יש צידנית → TRANSFER_TO_COOLER` — has NO temperature floor, NO category ban and NO cumulative-exposure budget. Route it through the approved Phase 3a §3.5 gate instead: hot-hold floor ≥60 °C · `dangerZoneMin(...) > 240` rejects · holdable = big-collagen cuts only · `holdCapMin` 360 min hard · solver ceiling `pref('holdMaxH')*60`. As written it will put chicken and fish in a cooler — §3.5's explicit "never holdable: lean cuts · anything served medium-rare · all poultry · all fish/seafood". (2) The claimed "שומרת מעל 60°C ל-4-8 שעות" is uncited and its upper bound EXCEEDS our own 360-min hard cap — drop the range, keep the cap. (3) Make it a kit entity with a real capacity, not an event boolean: a cooler has area and holds a finite number of cuts, and a boolean cannot answer "do both briskets fit".

adapt.item: Device failure as a first-class event that triggers a re-solve (§5.5 `handleDeviceFailure`, backup ladder: free oven → covered grill → FAILED).
adapt.why: We have nothing here. `schedulePlacements` runs once at `buildList()` time; if a smoker dies at hour 6 of a 12-hour cook, nothing re-solves. The ladder's insight is sound and specific — "גיבוי 1: תנור פנוי → העברה (הבשר כבר ספג עשן)": once smoke has been absorbed an oven is a legitimate substitute, a real culinary fact that makes the fallback principled rather than merely convenient. Cheap for us: `cookerCandidates(kind)` already returns the substitute set (it already appends `equipByCat('oven')` for `cook` stages), and `schedulePlacements` is a pure function we can re-run against a reduced `equipList()`.
adapt.whatMustChange: The proposal's ladder ignores the two device checks we already have and must keep: `deviceCanReach(dev, tempC)` (a fallback oven that cannot reach the stage temperature is a refusal, not a re-schedule — `reason:'temp-ceiling'`) and the per-slot/hook/bath fit (a fallback that cannot physically hold the item is not a fallback). A mid-cook re-solve must also never alter any stage's `temp`/`hours`/`safe` — that is DoD-10, and we already have the runtime invariant for it (`window._planSafetyViolations` via `safetyDiff`, app.js:7091-7100); the re-solve must live inside that fence. Belongs in Phase 3b (live re-solving), not 3a.

adapt.item: The consumables consumption RATES (§6.4: offset ~1.5 kg wood/hr, charcoal cabinet ~0.8 kg/hr + 2 wood chunks/hr, pellet 1.0/2.0 kg/hr, butcher paper ~1.5 m per wrapped item).
adapt.why: The output shape is adoptable (see ADOPT); the numbers are asserted with no source anywhere in the document — in a project where `sources.py` carries 279 citations merged at build time.
adapt.whatMustChange: Treat every rate as unsourced until traced. These are not `safe` values so DoD-10 does not literally bind them, but the same discipline should: a fuel underestimate strands a live cook. Either cite them (manufacturer burn-rate specs, pellet-hopper consumption tables) or ship them explicitly labelled as estimates with the ×1.2 buffer and no false precision. Do not copy the table.

reject.item: `EventOptimizationEngine.optimizeEvent` as a replacement for, or basis of, our scheduler (§5.2).
reject.defect: It is not an optimizer. No contention detection, no re-planning, and no interaction between its spatial and temporal passes; adopting it would delete every capability our placer already ships.
reject.evidence: The whole time loop: `for (let item of menu) { let cookEndTime = ...; let cookStartTime = ...; scheduleTimeline.push({...}); }` — `equipment` appears nowhere inside it. Compare `schedulePlacements` (app.js:3969-4057), which emits seven distinct typed conflicts — `temp-ceiling`, `hooks`, `bath-temp`, `bath-too-small`, `no-single-slot`, `no-window`, `pull-too-far` — none of which has any counterpart in v5.0. v5.0's only failure mode is `throw new Error('חסימת נפח: אין מקום עבור [...]')`, refusing the whole event rather than naming the item and the shortfall.

reject.defect: Generates sous-vide DURATIONS by multiplying a smoking time — and for sous-vide, duration IS a safety value, because pasteurization is a function of time × temperature. The proposal states this itself and violates it two sections later. It is also dimensionally wrong: sous-vide time at a fixed temperature depends on thickness and the pasteurization/collagen tables, not on how long the cut takes in a pit. Two briskets that take 8 h and 14 h in a pit take the SAME time at 68 °C.
reject.evidence: §4.1 Rule 2: `פסטור = פונקציה של טמפרטורה × זמן; חום נמוך מחייב הארכת זמן.` §4.4: `SET TIME_CONVERSION_FACTOR = 2.5    // הארכה פי 2.5`. It also contradicts its own §3.2, which hard-codes `TRIGGER_NEXT_STAGE_WHEN = (TIME_ELAPSED == 24_HOURS)` regardless of the source smoke time. Directly opposed to OUR-SYSTEM-BRIEF §2, verified in code: `itemPaths(meta)` enumerates "כל צירופי המסלולים המצוטטים (cited-only, לעולם לא נוסחתי)".

reject.item: The cooler-transfer and crisis rules in the telemetry loop (§5.5 / §6.3) as written.
reject.defect: A hold with no minimum temperature, no cumulative danger-zone budget and no category ban. `TRANSFER_TO_COOLER` fires on `הגעה ליעד + זמן עד הגשה > מנוחה + יש צידנית` — nothing in that condition excludes poultry or fish, and nothing tracks accumulated sub-60 °C time. `CRISIS_SPEED_UP` raises chamber temperature by 15 °C with no ceiling check.
reject.evidence: Phase 3a §3.5 already specifies the opposite and calls the floors "never knobs, never AI-decided": hot-hold floor ≥60 °C · danger-zone ≤240 min cumulative · `holdCapMin` 360 min hard · `never holdable: lean cuts · anything served medium-rare · all poultry · all fish/seafood`. On the temperature raise: `deviceCanReach(dev, tempC)` (app.js:3963) exists precisely because "a 160 °C stage could sit on a 135 °C electric smoker with nothing said", and `occupancyCompat`'s `setpoint` carries an explicit fence — "It must NEVER be written back onto a stage's `temp`: that would raise a lower-temp cut above its recipe temperature, a food-safety violation. Fenced by tests/setpoint-fence.spec."

reject.item: Moving the rules engine into a Cloudflare Worker (§9.2: `Cloudflare Worker = מנוע החוקים v5.0`).
reject.defect: The solver is a pure, millisecond-scale function of local state; a Worker adds a network round-trip to every timeline rebuild, an offline failure mode on the primary surface, and — the real cost — a SECOND copy of the safety data that can drift from `sources.py`'s 279 citations, outside the reach of the build-time Guards.
reject.evidence: Phase 3a §3.1 specifies `orchestrate` as "Pure function over the already-computed schedule. No DOM, no storage writes." `planSchedule`/`schedulePlacements` are likewise pure. `buildList()` (app.js:7035) re-runs the whole computation on every UI interaction. And Guards A/B/C run at build time over the inlined bundle only (`build.py`) — safety numbers living in a separately-deployed Worker would be enforced by nothing. Our existing Worker (`worker/index.js`, 91 lines) is deliberately a thin Gemini proxy running no culinary logic; keep it that way.

reject.defect: Uncited multipliers that nothing consumes — returned in the payload as `smoke_intensity_multiplier: smokeIntensityAdjustment` and read by no code anywhere in the document.
reject.evidence: A computed value with no reader is exactly what our DoD-5 forbids: "Any new derived/computed value has a real reader in production code, named here... a reader that never executes is still dead."

reject.item: `if (meat.weight_kg * 3 > (equipment.vessel_capacity_liters || 0)) throw` as the sous-vide capacity model (§4.5).
reject.defect: An uncited 3 L/kg factor; single-item only; no notion of two items sharing one bath, and therefore no temperature-exclusivity rule at all. Strictly weaker than what we ship.
reject.evidence: `eqmFitVerdict`'s volume branch (equipment.js:255+) takes the MAX not the sum — with the reason stated in `deviceOccupancy`: "min_bath_l is each item's REQUIRED bath size (a per-item constraint), NOT additive displacement — summing it produced a false 'over' for items that share one bath" — and gates sharing on exact temperature equality: "only demands that CITE a tempC must agree with one another... strict `!==` is the correct equality test here; no epsilon is needed or wanted". `EQM.allocate` carries `tempC` into the held ledger entry so the check has something real to compare against, and `schedulePlacements` emits `reason:'bath-temp'` and `reason:'bath-too-small'` separately.

reject.defect: Sorts a locale-formatted display string instead of a timestamp; breaks across the day boundary, which is the normal case for this product's flagship 8–14 h cooks.
reject.evidence: §3.3's own table gives brisket 8-14 h and pork shoulder 10-14 h. Our code handles the rollover deliberately: `app.js:7020` `// pick the serve day (night / next-day cooks)`, plus `fmtClockRel(preheat, serve)` for relative-day rendering. I did not verify the exact ICU output of `toLocaleTimeString('he-IL', ...)` under RTL (it may also carry direction marks), so I rest the objection on the day boundary alone, which is unambiguous.

impactOnUs:
**If we adopt v5.0's §5 as an engine: nothing improves and a great deal regresses.** There is no path where `optimizeEvent` replaces `planSchedule` (app.js:3858) + `schedulePlacements` (app.js:3969) without losing per-stage scheduling, slack-based earlier-pull (app.js:7075-7089), the typed conflict reasons consumed by `_schedAdviceHtml(window._plcConflicts, computed)` (app.js:7121), `packDevice`'s time-aware shelf reuse (app.js:528), `deviceCanReach`'s temperature-ceiling refusal (app.js:3963), hook capacity, and bath-temperature exclusivity. `tests/contention-per-slot.spec.ts`, `tests/occ-fit-ladder.spec.ts`, `tests/occ-setpoint-delta.spec.ts`, `tests/setpoint-fence.spec.ts`, `tests/e2-availability.spec.ts` and `tests/e2-allocate-release.spec.ts` all assert behaviour with no counterpart in the proposal. My recommendation: change nothing in the scheduler.

**If we take the three harvests, here is what actually changes.**

1. **Cooler/hold vessel.** Amend `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-17-cookout-orchestrator-phase3a-design.md` §3.3 (the `hold` move) and §3.5 to name a *holding vessel* with a capacity, and add it as an equipment category alongside the existing `EQUIP_CATS` in `equipment_map.py`/`equipment.js`. Then `SCHED_PULL_MAX_MS` (app.js:3945) stops being a bare constant and becomes a function of whether a vessel with room exists for the whole waiting window; `schedulePlacements`'s `reason:'pull-too-far'` branch gains a second outcome ("pull further, hold in the cooler") instead of only refusing. `safetyGate` in §3.5 is the gate for it — unchanged, reused.

2. **Device-failure re-plan.** Phase 3b, not now. Concretely: re-run `schedulePlacements(computed, scope)` against `equipList()` minus the failed device, diff the placements, and route substitutes through `cookerCandidates(kind)` — all inside the existing `safetyDiff`/`window._planSafetyViolations` fence (app.js:7091-7100).

3. **Consumables.** A new pure function over `schedulePlacements(...).placements`, rendered near `workPlanHtml` (app.js:7118). Touches `equipPlan`'s neighbourhood (it already computes `fuelNote`/`refuelEveryMin`) and closes part of gap D4. Every new string must go through `L(he, en)` with static literals or Guard A fails the build, and any number+unit in it must survive Guard B's unit classes.

**One bug the proposal indirectly exposes, in our code, today.** v5.0 correctly subtracts rest before cook (`serve − resting − cook`). We model rest as a real stage (`restMin` per profile at app.js:3709-3730; `stages.push({label:'מנוחה', hours:p.restMin/60, kind:'rest'})` at app.js:4164), so the backward walk is right. But the LIVE side is not: `copilotPace` computes `const readyBy = s.serveTs - (s.restMin||0)*60000` (app.js:6796) while `restMin` is never written into the session object created by `startLiveCook` (app.js:6740: `{startedAt, scope, serveTs, probes:[]}`). The live ahead/on-pace/behind verdict therefore always assumes zero rest. This is gap **B15** in `docs/analysis/2026-07-27-gap-closing-BIG-STATUS.md` ("Copilot reserves no rest and follows the wrong event", OPEN) — confirmed still true in the code. A shipped surface giving a wrong answer, and roughly a one-line fix at `startLiveCook`.

risks.risk: The cooler-transfer rule is implemented as the proposal writes it, without the Phase 3a §3.5 floors. Chicken or fish held in an insulated box; no cumulative danger-zone tracking exists anywhere in the app today.
risks.mitigation: Hard sequencing: no cooler/hold work of any kind ships before Phase 3a slice 3 lands `safetyGate`, `holdable()`, `holdCapMin()` and `dangerZoneMin()`. Every hold path routes through `safetyGate` — no second code path. Test 7 in the 3a testing plan already specifies the negative cases (poultry never yields a hold; >6 h dropped; >240 danger-zone minutes dropped) — write those RED first.

risks.risk: The §4.4 conversion factors are treated as engine constants and generate sous-vide durations. Duration is a pasteurization variable; a 2.5× multiple of a smoke time has no relationship to a safe hold-at-temperature time.
risks.mitigation: Reject outright. `itemPaths` stays cited-only. If method conversion is ever wanted as a feature, each converted duration must come from `sources.py` (Baldwin tables) like every other duration, and the DoD-10 invariant (`safetyDiff` over `{kind,hours,temp,safe}`) must cover it.

risks.risk: The rules engine is moved server-side, creating a second copy of safety data outside the build-time Guards. `sources.py`'s 279 citations and Guards A/B/C only bind what `build.py` inlines.
risks.mitigation: Keep the solver client-side and pure, as Phase 3a §3.1 already specifies. If server-side rule evaluation ever becomes necessary, the data must be GENERATED from `data.py`/`sources.py` at build time and shipped to the Worker as an artifact, never hand-maintained — and the Guards must run over that artifact.

risks.risk: The 60%-of-cook-time wrap estimate reaches a user surface while `copilotStallInfo`'s temperature model (65–77 °C) drives another. Two surfaces give two different wrap instructions.
risks.mitigation: Do not import `action_wrap_stall`. This is exactly the cross-surface contradiction class CP1 just closed by making `itemStages` the single stage authority — any wrap instruction must come from there.

risks.risk: Supabase is taken on for IoT ingestion and its free tier pauses the project on inactivity, silently breaking a telemetry endpoint mid-cook. I could not verify current free-tier pause behaviour from here and am not asserting it as fact.
risks.mitigation: Verify current tier terms before committing. Note we already operate a Cloudflare Worker with KV (`worker/index.js`), so a Worker + KV/Durable Object path may cover server-side polling and push without introducing a second vendor — that comparison should be made explicitly rather than defaulting to the proposal's stack.

risks.risk: §6.1's premise — polling Meater/Inkbird/ThermoWorks clouds from an edge function — may not be available. The document itself calls these closed ecosystems ("אקו-סיסטם סגור") and then proposes integrating with their clouds anyway, citing no API.
risks.mitigation: Before any infrastructure decision rests on IoT: confirm at least one named vendor publishes a documented third-party API with terms permitting it. If none does, options (b) file upload and (c) manual override remain — and (c) is what we already ship (`liveSession().probes` + `copilotPace`), which removes the server requirement entirely.

risks.risk: Harvest work is pulled forward and displaces the approved sequence. The orchestrator (charter P8) is last by design because it needs P3+P5.
risks.mitigation: Amend the Phase 3a spec now (an owner decision under the §4 Waiver Gate either way) and build nothing now. Ship CP2 → E4 → CP3 → CP4 → E5/E6 as planned; the harvests land with P8. The one exception worth considering separately is the B15 rest bug, a live defect independent of all of this.

costEstimate:
**Rejecting v5.0's §5 optimizer: zero.** We keep `planSchedule` + `schedulePlacements` + `packDevice` + `cookerContention` exactly as shipped. No test churn, no risk. The cheapest decision in the document.

**The three harvests, if approved:**
- *Cooler/hold vessel* — **medium**, and it should be folded INTO Phase 3a slice 3 (`v252`: wood + hold + danger-zone accumulator + AI ranking) rather than made a separate slice. It adds a kit category, a capacity check reusing `eqmFitVerdict`, and turns `SCHED_PULL_MAX_MS` into a computed bound. Roughly +25–35% on slice 3, mostly in tests: the negative cases (poultry, over-cap, danger-zone overrun) are the bulk of the work and the reason to do it at all.
- *Device-failure re-plan* — **large**, and it belongs in Phase 3b (live re-solving), which has no spec yet. The code is cheap because `schedulePlacements` is pure and re-runnable; the expensive parts are the live-state model, "what has already happened is immutable", and the UI for a mid-cook plan change.
- *Consumables predictor* — **small-to-medium in code; the real cost is sourcing.** Independent of everything else, could ship at any point. Budget most of it for tracing burn rates to manufacturer specs rather than copying the proposal's table.

**Displacement.** The current map is CP2 → E4 → CP3 → CP4 → E5/E6 → orchestrator (P8), with P8 deliberately last (charter D1: needs P3+P5). None of the harvests justifies reordering it. The honest recommendation: **spend nothing now except a spec amendment** to Phase 3a §3.3/§3.5 naming the holding vessel, so the idea is captured while the spec is still open rather than retrofitted after the solver is built. Amending an approved spec is an owner decision under §4 — this note is the raising of it.

The one item I would spend on immediately, and it is not from the proposal: the **B15 rest bug** (`restMin` never written to the live session, so `copilotPace`'s ahead/behind verdict assumes zero rest). Small, on a shipped surface, currently wrong.
openQuestions: Is a cooler / faux-cambro a piece of EQUIPMENT (kit registry, with a real capacity, like every other device) or an event-level boolean as the proposal has it (`events.has_cooler_box`)? It has an area and holds a finite number of cuts, so the kit registry is the natural home — but it is not a cooker, so `cookerCandidates()` would never return it and it needs a category the placer treats differently from a heat source. This modelling decision determines whether `SCHED_PULL_MAX_MS` can become a computed bound.

Is real IoT (Meater / Inkbird / ThermoWorks cloud polling) an actual product goal, or is manual probe entry the intended UX? Nearly the entire infrastructure case in this document rests on that answer. Today we ship manual entry (`liveSession().probes` + `copilotPace`'s two-point ETA projection with an ahead/on-pace/behind verdict) and it needs no server at all.

Background push is the one server-side capability we demonstrably lack, and the app admits it in its own toast: `'התראות פעילות — השאר את האפליקציה פתוחה (המסך יישאר דלוק). התראות רקע אינן מובטחות'` (app.js:7027), with a wake lock as the workaround. For a 12-hour brisket that is a genuine product weakness. Is fixing it worth taking on server-side infrastructure — and if so, Supabase, or a scheduled Cloudflare Worker + Web Push given we already run a Worker at no cost?

Does the citation discipline extend to NON-safety operational numbers — fuel burn rates, metres of butcher paper, cooler hold duration? DoD-10 binds `safe`, `temp` and cook duration. A fuel underestimate is not a food-safety failure but it does strand a live cook. I would apply the same discipline; making that explicit decides whether the consumables feature is a week or a month.

Should the cooler, once modelled, change the SHAPE of the placer's refusal? Today `pull-too-far` (>2 h) is an honest refusal to reschedule.
